title: Talladega College, then Detroit and the first club dates
summary: After one year of music major at Talladega, Wilson went to Detroit in summer 1929, joined Local 5 and worked club dates with Howard Bunch and Everett Barksdale.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Uh huh. So we know you've been at Tuskegee and then Talladega and all this. Now when did you first start to go and make gigs and do a little playing? What kind of groups did you go out with?

That would have been in Detroit late in the year, 1929. I went to college one year in Talladega, took a music major there under a very talented man named Tergee Debolis (phonetic) -- an excellent classical pianist and a master of harmony, and really knew how to teach the students the basic things that we really should know about music.
But that term began in the Fall of '28, and I

left in the Spring, at the end of that term, I guess around June of 1929, and that summer, went to Detroit and never went back to school. And joined the union in Detroit and just started club-dating around Detroit.
What was the local there in Detroit?

Yeah. And I started doing club dates with people like Howard Bunce and an especially good friend of mine in those days, he was very helpful to me -- I don't know exactly how I met him, maybe it was through Howard Bunce, was Everett Barksdale, a guitarist. He's a very busy guitar player in Detroit in those days, and he put in a good word for me and my brother.
I guess we're getting to be around when I was about 17 years old in those days.
